reviews.review:
Space Marine's biggest achievement is knowing what a Warhammer 40k marine is and how to make the player feel like one - it's linear story still got the standard beats and it feels kinda sparse in variation sometimes, but the singleplayer experience is still pretty good.

For those that don't know Warhammer 40.000 setting is a "gothic space opera" so space marines are both classic space troopers, and simultaneously monastic order knights with decorated armors fighting things like demons and armed orcs. Demons, too, are sometimes armed with guns. They're two-meter tall superhumans fueled by devotion. This game nails it quite some with regular human combatants looking like children beside you, and you get to brutally beat enemies in melee not just shoot them, and the campaign has sections when you get gear like jetpacks to leap into crowds of enemies from up high.

Since then there were more games that really delivered on what it means to be a space marine but at a time this was probably the most hands on experience in this setting, only other successful and loved WH40k videogame being an RTS title, also from Relic. Nowadays you get top down and sidescroller and boomer shooter marine games. Honestly comparing to them this one is solid but somewhat by the numbers.

One thing I must note that I got this either in a bundle or for free ages ago and that the current default prices is criminal to a game that didn't age most gracefully despite otherwise being nice, so I insist only grab this at a real big sale or a bundle somewhere. Also, multiplayer is most definitely dead, no need to check.
amazing game from the 360 era. gameplay holds up nice. will be a great intro for the second one coming out in september '24. for the emperror!

First, I absolutely do not recommend this game at full price. It is basically a 60fps version of a 13 year old game. But at a discount, it's worth it. 

This game is a fairly clear 7/10, but there's nothing else really like it, and that works in its favour. Also, it is a surprising part of video game history - more on that in a moment. You play as a "space marine" that has to repel an "ork" invasion, almost singlehandedly. It really delivers on the "power fantasy" if that's your thing. You feel slow and heavy, and while shooting and melee combat (and movement for that matter) both feel clunky, they're also very satisfying. So, you "rip and tear" your way through hordes of foes. That allusion is not accidental - this game seems to have pioneered the glory kill system that came to define the play of Doom 2016. No spoilers for the story, but the plots are also very similar. It's pretty remarkable that a AA Warhammer spinoff became so influential on game design. Finally, be advised that the game is really short. I beat it in just over 6 hours, and that's with picking up most of the collectibles.
A bonkers adaptation of the 40k IP. A shame the multiplayer is dead. Get keen for the sequel.
